wa_direct_north_buttress.belay: In a recessed spot at the base of the next crack and corner system, reached by climbing the cracks.
wa_direct_north_buttress.notes: From the toe of the buttress, go right up slabs, then trend left into a broken slabby wall seamed with cracks. Climb the cracks to a recessed belay. The rock low on the buttress is poor in places; the couloir to the left is the loose, rockfall-prone alternative this start avoids.

wa_direct_north_buttress.belay: On a small ledge just above the roof, once you have pulled through it.
wa_direct_north_buttress.notes: Climb the crack in the dihedral to a roof. The crack widens toward the roof; stay in it until below the roof, then move out right, where a good hold helps. Pull through to a small ledge belay. A #4 cam is the piece that makes this pitch comfortable.
Continue up the corner system to the base of a chimney, then climb the chimney system; the two pitches can be linked. Stacked flakes lead into the chimney, so test before weighting.

Traverse left past loose blocks, which is the most unpleasant ground on the route, then back right through thin cracks with sparse protection. Ledge systems and easy but poorly protected ground follow. Protect the follower on the traverses and keep the rope clear of loose blocks.

Climb the ridge toward the snow patch; the rock here is often wet from melt. Beyond the snow, climb the face behind it by a left-hand crack to join the original 1967 North Buttress line. Crampons are recommended and a light axe helps for the snow.

wa_direct_north_buttress.belay: On a ledge up on the crest of the buttress, at the top of the corner.
wa_direct_north_buttress.notes: A strenuous left-facing corner with a crack running from hands to fists, steep and sustained for much of a long pitch. The rock quality improves markedly from here up. Bring wide hand and fist sizes.
Two pitches up the buttress crest to the ledge at the base of the offwidth, where the 1967 party bivouacked.

16a climbs the offwidth, awkward with a pack, past some fixed gear; it is graded from 5.10a to 5.10-. 16b is the bypass: start up the offwidth, then trend right around the corner onto easier ground at about 5.8 and belay above the wide section.
Climb the buttress crest on steep, airy face holds with big exposure. Belay below the long crack system above.

wa_direct_north_buttress.belay: On a small stance at the top of the long series of thin cracks.
wa_direct_north_buttress.notes: A long series of thin cracks, close to a full rope length, to a small stance. The rock here is lichen-covered; expect it to feel harder when damp.

Easier blocky ground up the buttress to the ridgeline. Many parties leave the rope here and move up Class 4 and easy 5th, trending right to the summit ridge. Descend west on Class 3-4 ground, then snow and cliff bands back to camp.
